channel.title: Quant Arena
channel.description: Weekly arena reports, research articles and site updates.

item.title: Auditable strategy evidence and direct engine positions
item.description: Six representative strategies now have evidence bundles on SPY, gold and bitcoin: full-precision daily accounting, simulated position changes, actual selected parameters, source hashes and a standalone arithmetic replay script. The evidence index preserves prior corrected snapshots. Signals now come from engine targets rather than ratios of rounded returns, with target and effective exposure, per-market observation dates and independent data status. The current UTC date is excluded conservatively. Walk-forward boundary returns are recomputed from the previous published target, and skipped folds retain default targets; the evidence index quantifies these accounting changes. This is an 18-pair pilot, not full-site verification or broker fills.

item.title: Quant Arena Weekly Report: week 2026-W45 (2026-11-02 – 2026-11-05)
item.description: What moved in the arena during the week ending 2026-11-05: market moves, strategies that changed position, and the best and worst performers over the last month.

item.title: New: AI Strategy Arena
item.description: Six trading rules written by an AI assistant, with every parameter fixed, are now tracked every trading day on nine markets against buy-and-hold and our 72 classic strategies. Because a language model may already know past markets, the ranking uses only results after 4 November 2026, the day the rules were frozen; the historical backtest is shown for reference only.

item.title: New: open-source trading frameworks directory
item.description: A guide to 18 widely used open-source projects for backtesting, live trading, crypto bots, machine learning and market data (Backtrader, vectorbt, LEAN, NautilusTrader, vn.py, Freqtrade, Qlib, FinRL, TradingAgents and more): what each is for, strengths, limitations, alternatives and seven head-to-head comparisons. GitHub stars, last commit, latest release and maintenance status are refreshed every week.

item.title: Subscribe to the weekly report
item.description: Every static page now has a subscribe box for the weekly Arena report (ranking changes, new signals and new research), sent by email through Buttondown. We also started counting anonymous usage events such as searches and comparisons with Umami, which uses no cookies.

item.title: A site map for AI assistants (llms.txt)
item.description: The site now publishes llms.txt, a plain-text guide for AI assistants and answer engines: what Quant Arena tests and how, the main pages, every live research article with its data date, the glossary and all strategy pages. It is rebuilt with the sitemap every day.

item.title: Out-of-sample check on strategy pages
item.description: Strategy pages now compare the Sharpe ratio that the walk-forward parameters had on their training windows with what they earned in the following six months, and with the default parameters over the same months. They also show how many settings in the parameter grid had a positive Sharpe ratio. Across the 486 strategy-and-market pairs with parameters to tune, the median Sharpe ratio fell from 0.32 on the training windows to 0.19 out of sample; the walk-forward glossary entry has the details.

item.title: EA backtests now cover the latest twelve months
item.description: All 1,063 converted EAs were re-run on four markets with hourly data from November 2025 to November 2026 (previously May 2025 to May 2026). 1,119 results are reliable enough to rank. This now happens automatically every month.

item.title: We Backtested 72 Strategies. After Adjusting for Luck, None Clearly Beat the Odds.
item.description: 104 strategy-and-market combinations look statistically convincing on their own. Once you account for the fact that we tested hundreds of them at the same time, the number drops to zero. Here is what that means for reading any leaderboard, including ours.

item.title: We Tried to Backtest 1,063 Free MT5 Expert Advisors. Here Is What Survived.
item.description: Free MetaTrader 5 EAs from the MQL5 CodeBase, converted automatically and tested on four markets for one year. More than half could not be converted at all. Of the 1,123 results we trust, about half made money — but on currencies the typical EA ended flat, only 30 EAs were profitable on all four markets, and one in five gold runs wiped out the account.

item.title: Which Trading Strategies Survived 2022? 62 Backtests Through Three Sell-offs
item.description: In the 2022 bear market SPY fell 24.5% from peak to trough. Every one of the 62 strategies we run on SPY lost less, and ten of them made money. Mean reversion held up best, momentum worst. Here is what the COVID crash and the late-2018 sell-off add to the picture.

item.title: Why Martingale and Grid EAs Blow Up: What 1,515 Free MT5 Expert Advisors and Their Losing Streaks Show
item.description: Martingale and grid EAs make up 5% of the free MT5 Expert Advisors we review, but more than half of the ones we rate "dangerous". The reason is arithmetic: losing streaks of six to eight trades are normal — and that is exactly where doubling the position runs out of money.

item.title: Do Moving-Average Strategies Still Work on Bitcoin? Nine Systems, Five Years
item.description: Over the last five years buy-and-hold bitcoin returned 7.2% a year with a 77% drawdown. Five of nine moving-average-style systems beat that return, and every one of them cut the worst drawdown. Over the full history the picture flips: almost nothing beats simply holding.

item.title: Does Turtle Trading Still Work? Ten Markets, 2021–2026
item.description: Two breakout systems, ten markets, five years. Neither beat buy-and-hold on most markets, but the slower Donchian version had a smaller drawdown on nine of ten, and both made money on commodities in the 2022 bear market when stocks fell 25%.

item.title: Does an RSI Filter Make MACD Better? A Ten-Market Test
item.description: Adding an RSI filter to a MACD crossover cut the maximum drawdown on nine of ten markets and reduced trading by 10–30%. It improved the Sharpe ratio on only five, and gave up return on the strongest trends — silver, bitcoin and ether.

item.title: Two Strategies, the Same 10% Drawdown, Very Different Pain: How to Read Drawdown, the Ulcer Index and Rolling Sharpe
item.description: Maximum drawdown tells you how deep the worst fall was, not how long you spent underwater or how often it happened. Two strategies on the S&P 500 with almost identical 10% drawdowns show why the Ulcer index and drawdown duration are worth a look — and why a single Sharpe ratio can mislead as much as a single drawdown.

item.title: Keltner Breakout or Bollinger Reversion? Ten Markets Split Down the Middle
item.description: Two volatility-band strategies that do opposite things: one buys when price breaks out of a Keltner Channel, the other buys when price falls to the lower Bollinger Band. Over the last five years each had the better Sharpe ratio on exactly five of ten markets — and the split follows a clear pattern: breakouts won where prices trended, reversion won where they went back and forth.

item.title: EA pages show results month by month
item.description: For each market with a reliable backtest, EA pages now show the share of months with a gain and the best and worst month, with dates. EA backtests are also re-run every month on the latest twelve months of hourly data.

item.title: Strategy results now always use walk-forward optimization
item.description: Until now, each strategy kept its default parameters whenever they scored better over the whole history than the walk-forward run. That choice looked at the full sample, so it flattered the results: it applied to 106 of 576 strategy-and-market results, which scored a median of 5.6 points higher than their walk-forward versions. Every result now uses walk-forward optimization, so some numbers and rankings moved down.

item.title: Identical EA backtests are no longer counted
item.description: 85 EAs produced exactly the same backtest as another EA on every market — for example 14 unrelated EAs with identical results — which means the automatic conversion lost what made them different. Their 298 results are now labeled "Same as other EAs", with links to the twins, and are left out of the EA Ranking, the category statistics and the blow-up risk evidence. Reliable EA results go from 1,421 to 1,123. The article on 1,063 free MT5 EAs and the glossary have been updated.

item.title: EA pages compare each EA with its category
item.description: Under the backtest table, EA pages now show how each result ranks against other EAs of the same category on the same market, for example "EURUSD: better than 82% of 37". Only reliable results count, and only when at least ten EAs of the category have one.

item.title: Two new glossary terms: recovery factor and blow-up risk
item.description: The glossary now has 20 terms. Recovery factor explains the number in the EA Ranking (the median EA backtest scored about zero). Blow-up risk explains broker stop-outs, how our backtests handle them and how the EA labels work: 61 of 307 gold backtests with default lot sizes ended in a stop-out, none on three currency pairs. EA pages link to both.

item.title: Blow-up risk label for every Expert Advisor
item.description: Each EA now carries a blow-up risk label built from its code and our backtests: martingale sizing, grid orders, no stop loss, several positions at once, and whether the account was stopped out in our backtest. The label shows on EA pages, in the EA Arena (with a filter), in the EA Ranking and on the category pages. 93 EAs are rated high, 66 elevated. EA categories in the app now match the EA pages.

item.title: A plain leaderboard page and a faster home page
item.description: The new leaderboard page lists the top 10 strategies on every market for the last 12 months and the last five years, in English and Chinese, without waiting for the app to load. The home page now shows its summary, top strategies and latest research straight away, and every static page links to the static versions of the leaderboard, strategy library, EA categories and info pages.

item.title: Readable pages for About, Methodology, FAQ and more
item.description: About, Methodology, FAQ, Changelog, Privacy and Terms now have plain HTML versions (English and Chinese) that load without JavaScript and are what search engines index. Tool views such as the EA ranking and the strategy lab are no longer offered to search engines.

item.title: Quant Arena Weekly Report: week 2026-W33 (2026-08-10 – 2026-08-14)
item.description: What moved in the arena during the week ending 2026-08-14: market moves, strategies that changed position, and the best and worst performers over the last month.

item.title: Donchian Channel and Turtle Breakout: Trading the 20/10 Rule
item.description: The Turtle system uses Donchian breakouts and risk based sizing to capture sustained trends. This research note explains the logic, market fit, and failure modes.

item.title: Supertrend and ATR Trailing Stop: Volatility Adjusted Trend Control
item.description: Supertrend uses ATR based bands to define trend flips and stops. This research note explains the signal mechanics, regime fit, and the risks of whipsaw.

item.title: Ichimoku Cloud Strategy: Regime, Momentum, and Support in One System
item.description: Ichimoku combines trend, momentum, and support into a single framework. This research note breaks down the components, signals, and common traps.

item.title: RSI Mean Reversion Strategy: Buying Weakness Inside Ranges
item.description: RSI mean reversion looks for short term exhaustion and then fades the move. This research note covers the signal logic, market fit, and risk traps.

item.title: EMA Crossover Strategy: Reading Trend With Two Clocks
item.description: An in depth look at why exponential moving average crossovers persist, how to interpret their backtests, and when trend signals fail.

item.title: Parabolic SAR Strategy: A Trend Exit Engine
item.description: Parabolic SAR uses a trailing stop that accelerates with trend strength. This article explains why it works, when it fails, and how to read its backtests.

item.title: Volatility Breakout Strategy: Trading Expansion Without Overreach
item.description: Volatility breakouts focus on price moves that escape a recent range. This guide explains the logic, the regimes where it works, and the traps to avoid.

item.title: How QuantArenas Ranks Strategies
item.description: A full methodology essay on why the Arena Score blends multiple metrics, how stability is measured, and how to read results without overfitting.
